title: A scalar-fraction criterion for a localization functor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal C$ an $R$-linear triangulated category with $R$-linear integer shifts [def-weil-linear-category], [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $M\subseteq R$ be a submonoid, let $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[M^{-1}]$ be [sk-def-sfb-rationalization], and let $\mathcal D$ be a preadditive $R$-linear category. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an additive $R$-linear functor [def-weil-linear-functor]. Suppose that $F$ is essentially surjective, inverts $W_M$, and $m\operatorname{id}_Y$ is invertible for every $m\in M$ and $Y\in\mathcal D$. Assume, for all $A,B\in\mathcal C$: (i) for every $h:FA\to FB$ there are $m\in M$ and $u:A\to B$ with $mh=F(u)$; (ii) if $F(u)=F(v)$ then $nu=nv$ for some $n\in M$. Then the induced functor $G:\mathcal C[M^{-1}]\to\mathcal D$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective, and $F$ is a localization at $W_M$ in the universal-property sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. No triangulated structure on $\mathcal D$ is required.

source.place: Morphisms of the rationalization, full faithfulness, and conclusion; generic algebraic assembly extracted by the agent

proof.text: Put $\mathcal L=\mathcal C[M^{-1}]$. By [sk-def-sfb-rationalization] and [def-weil-triangulated-category], $Q$ is an additive localization and every $m\in M$ acts invertibly on $\mathcal L$. By [lem-sfb-additive-localization-linear], its canonical linear structure satisfies $Q(ru)=rQ(u)$, and every $X\in\mathcal L$ is isomorphic to some $QA$.

source.place: Morphisms of the rationalization: additive linear localization and object representatives

proof.text: Since $F$ inverts $W_M$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives $G:\mathcal L\to\mathcal D$ and $\eta:GQ\xrightarrow{\sim}F$. Step 1 and the additive linear hypothesis on $F$ satisfy [lem-sfb-linear-localization-descent], hence $G(r\alpha)=rG(\alpha)$.

source.place: Full faithfulness: lift F and descend scalar preservation

proof.text: Fix $A,B$. Take $U=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)$, $V=\operatorname{Hom}(QA,QB)$, $W=\operatorname{Hom}(FA,FB)$ and $i=Q$, $j=F$ on arrows. Define $t(\alpha)=\eta_B G(\alpha)\eta_A^{-1}$. Naturality gives $ti=j$; bilinearity [def-weil-linear-category] and step 2 give $t(r\alpha)=rt(\alpha)$. Multiplication by $m\in M$ on $V,W$ is postcomposition by $m\operatorname{id}_{QB},m\operatorname{id}_{FB}$, with inverse postcomposition by their inverses. Thus it is bijective. Clause 1 of [lem-sfb-rationalization-scalar-fractions] gives fraction representatives in $V$; (i) gives them in $W$ and (ii) detects equal $j$-images. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-scalar-fraction-comparison-bijective] hold. Hence $t$ is bijective; conjugation by $\eta$ is bijective, so $G$ is fully faithful on $QA,QB$.

source.place: Full faithfulness: apply the module comparison to the conjugated Hom maps

proof.text: For arbitrary $X,Y$, choose $e:QA\cong X$, $d:QB\cong Y$. The bijection $a\mapsto d^{-1}ae$ on source Hom sets and its inverse $b\mapsto dbe^{-1}$ correspond, by functoriality, to the same bijections using $G(d),G(e)$ on target Hom sets. Step 3 therefore gives full faithfulness everywhere. For $Z\in\mathcal D$, choose $FA\cong Z$ by essential surjectivity of $F$; composing with $\eta_A:GQA\cong FA$ proves essential surjectivity of $G$.

source.place: Full faithfulness and essential surjectivity: explicit conjugation from image objects

proof.text: In a common sufficiently large universe, [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] applied to step 4 gives an equivalence with functor $G$. Apply [lem-sfb-localization-equivalent-target] to $Q$, this equivalence and $\eta:GQ\cong F$. It gives the full localization universal property for $F$. No triangles on $\mathcal D$ were used.

source.place: Conclusion: equivalence of G and transfer of the functor-category localization property
